messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Not quite: I want a fair financial share, and I haven’t agreed to a discounted sale. B’s needs should be heard, but I don’t know that she needs money. A fair price matters; there’s no real rush. I’m not sure what the will says about the split.
I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. We haven’t settled on a price or terms, and C’s agreement is needed; she hasn’t agreed yet.

Thank you. Yes, money is a concern—I’d like to use my share to start a dance studio. I don’t know what the house is worth or what the will means for each of us, so I’m not sure what amount might be possible. I’d like that included in the list.

I support finding out what the will says and agreeing on an independent appraiser. I can’t confirm A knows my agreement is needed. Please note that I won’t subsidize a discounted purchase; I want a fair financial share. No rush from me.

Yes, I’d support clarifying the will and choosing an independent appraiser together. By a family discount, I mean a price below the appraised value; we haven’t decided how much below. It matters because buying the house would help me build financial independence with my husband.
Yes, that seems sensible. I don’t have a set timeline for the studio, but I’d like to move forward when we know what funds may be available.

I could consider options one or two, depending on the figures and terms. I’m open to option three only if it’s legally workable and the numbers are clear. I’d prefer to buy the house, so option four would be a fallback, not my choice. I can’t yet say which option works best for everyone.

Option one could work, once we know the will’s split and the appraisal. I’m not agreeing to staged payments without clear terms that protect my share. Option three is acceptable if A can’t buy at a fair price. There’s no need to rush.

I could live with option one if my share is paid out clearly; option four could also work. Under option two, getting my share in parts would make planning for the studio harder, so I’d need clear timing. Option three might be workable if any discount doesn’t reduce my share, but that needs to be confirmed.
Yes, that plan works for me, subject to confirming the will, appraisal, and whether I can finance the purchase at that value. Any discount from my share can stay open pending legal advice.

It works, provided any discount comes solely from A’s share and doesn’t reduce mine or B’s. We should confirm the will and appraisal first. Any staged payments need clear terms protecting both our shares.
Yes, that plan works for me, as long as my share and any payment timing are clearly confirmed.
